building_stock: The only two South Melbourne-specific job signals returned are both retrofits onto existing doors rather than new-build hardware: an apartment main entry door in South Melbourne needing a supplied-and-installed McGrath ML-Windsor digital lock (Airtasker, Melbourne lock-installation page), and a Yale smart lock going onto a "standard door" that the poster expects to need a circular drill/jigsaw and chisel work to fit (Airtasker, Inner South Melbourne lock-installation page) — so expect a mix of shared apartment entry doors and plain existing timber doors that must be cut to accept the new lock body.
council_notes: No heritage overlay or council planning signal was returned; the regulatory constraint the records actually evidence is building-level and licensing-level — smartlockinstallation.com.au advertises being "assigned to" specific named VIC apartment developments (Aurora Central, The Parkhouse, Yarra One, Montague Square, Victoriana, Melbourne Square, Park Lane), i.e. installers are appointed per building, and the South Melbourne resident on Airtasker specifically stipulated "a licensed locksmith" for their apartment's main entry door.

common_concerns: Whether the installer is allowed to touch an apartment's main entry door at all — the returned records show installers advertising per-building appointments to named VIC developments (smartlockinstallation.com.au) and a South Melbourne resident insisting on a licensed locksmith for their apartment main entry door (Airtasker), so building/owners-corporation sign-off and licensing are the first questions asked.

Whether a specific model the customer has already chosen or bought can be fitted — both South Melbourne-area requests name the exact product (a McGrath ML-Windsor digital lock, a Yale smart lock), and one asks for supply-and-install while the other is install-only on a lock already in hand (Airtasker, Melbourne and Inner South Melbourne pages).

Irreversible cutting into an existing door — the Inner South Melbourne request spells out that the job "will need a circular drill/jigsaw, chisel and tools for assembly" (Airtasker), so customers here are aware the door gets modified and want to know it will be done cleanly.

Choosing between smart lock types before committing — smartlocksmelbourne.au's installation-service page frames the decision as "three main types of smart (digital) door lock" and Corporate Locksmiths lists smart keypads, lever locks, slim locks and smart deadbolts as separate options, and a smart-lock showroom at 59-61 Park St, South Melbourne is open only Monday to Friday 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM (mysmartlocks.com.au), so product selection advice is sought as part of the install booking.
